metadata.goal: Analyze mobility patterns around intermediate stops in daily trip chains.
metadata.category: Complete connected daily chains with intermediate-stop area, activity, duration, subsequent purpose and distance, transport mode, and timestamped trajectory points.
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 23 Intermediate Stop Daily Chain Patterns
metadata.dataset_description: Complete connected daily chains with intermediate-stop area, activity, duration, subsequent purpose and distance, transport mode, and timestamped trajectory points.
metadata.metric_note: Distances and directness are calculated from delivered GPS polylines; point speeds, trip durations, chain timing, and paired-leg timing are synchronized with the supplied point table. Route directness ratio is route distance divided by straight-line distance, so it is at least 1 and lower values indicate more direct routes.

plot.title: Intermediate-stop Variety by Area
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Which area types host the widest range of intermediate-stop activities, and how do those stops connect to following trips including return home?
insight_list.insight: Mixed-use areas host the widest variety of intermediate stops, connecting work, shopping, dining, and return-home trips within the same daily chains.

plot.title: Stop Timing, Duration, and Follow-up
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: What commonly follows short midday stops, and which activities account for longer stops across the daytime?
insight_list.insight: Short midday stops are commonly followed by shopping or dining trips, while longer daytime stops more often separate work-related movements.

plot.title: Stop Duration and Subsequent Change
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How does stop duration relate to changes in next-trip distance, purpose, and mode?
insight_list.insight: Longer stop durations are associated with larger changes in subsequent trip distance and purpose, while transport mode often remains unchanged.

insights: Mixed-use areas host the widest variety of intermediate stops, connecting work, shopping, dining, and return-home trips within the same daily chains.
Short midday stops are commonly followed by shopping or dining trips, while longer daytime stops more often separate work-related movements.
Longer stop durations are associated with larger changes in subsequent trip distance and purpose, while transport mode often remains unchanged.
summary: Mixed-use areas host the broadest intermediate-stop activity mix. Short midday stops commonly lead to shopping or dining, whereas longer daytime stops separate work-related movements and precede larger changes in distance and purpose; modes usually persist.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this controlled constructed dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
